text: This penguin pays one hundred eighty fish a month for this igloo.
And this walrus collects it.
But here's the thing.
The walrus never paid for the igloo.
He borrowed the fish from the bank.
Now he owes the bank one hundred fifty fish every month.
So he finds a penguin.
And rents him the igloo for one hundred eighty.
Every month, the penguin pays the walrus.
The walrus pays the bank.
The seagull takes his tax.
And the walrus keeps the rest.
Next year, the walrus raises the rent to two hundred.
The penguin's paycheck? Still the same.
This is called rent.
Thirty years later, the igloo is paid off.
Who paid for it?
The penguin.
Who owns it?
The walrus.
And the penguin owns...
one fish.
And the walrus? He just bought another igloo.
So should the penguin keep renting, or buy his own igloo? Tell me in the comments.
